authors: Eugène Bourgogne and Hippolyte Claude Pouilliart (Bourgogne Frères)
title: Préparations microscopiques d’anatomie animale et végétale
citation: Bourgogne Frères, “Préparations microscopiques d’anatomie animale et végétale,” in Catalogue officiel, Section française, International Exhibition, London (1862), 127–128.
tags: France; Paris; Bourgogne Frères; commercial preparations; exhibition; workshop; animal anatomy; botany
note: The official French-section catalogue describes a workshop founded in 1860 and a display devoted directly to animal- and plant-anatomy microscopic preparations. The partnership received an Honourable Mention. This is a dated commercial-production state distinct from Joseph Bourgogne's already-listed 1862 catalogue.

title: Préparations microscopiques d’objets d’anatomie et de botanique
citation: Bourgogne and C. Alliot, exhibition entry for microscopic preparations, Exposition Universelle de Paris, Catalogue général, Classe 12 (Paris, 1867), 62.
tags: France; Paris; Bourgogne; Alliot; commercial preparations; exhibition; anatomy; botany; medal
note: A slide-specific exhibition record for the Bourgogne–Alliot partnership. Contemporary exhibition documentation describes microscopic anatomical and botanical preparations and records the firm's Bronze Medal, providing a dated bridge between workshop identity and exhibited slide production.

title: Une lettre de M. Eug. Bourgogne, fabricant de préparations pour le microscope
citation: Eugène Bourgogne, “Une lettre de M. Eug. Bourgogne, fabricant de préparations pour le microscope,” Journal de la Société impériale et centrale d’horticulture de France (1868): 517.
tags: France; Paris; Eugène Bourgogne; botanical slides; vine; aphids; sectioning; applied microscopy
note: Bourgogne describes preparations of aphid-attacked grape vines cut in several directions to show both insect development and deterioration of the wood. The item is admitted because a professional slide-maker explains what his physical preparations were designed to make visible.
links: Bourgogne reconstruction with full periodical reference: https://www.microscopist.net/BourgogneJoseph.html

title: Préparations microscopiques d'anatomie et de physiologie des deux règnes organisés de la nature
citation: Joseph Bourgogne, catalogue of Préparations microscopiques d'anatomie et de physiologie des deux règnes organisés de la nature (Paris, 1874).
tags: France; Paris; Joseph Bourgogne; slide catalogue; commercial preparations; anatomy; physiology; trade
note: A later dedicated Bourgogne preparation catalogue, issued after his move to 2 Rue Pascal. It documents a mature commercial collection of mounted preparations and is retained separately from the already-listed 1862 catalogue as a later state of the business.

title: Microscope-slide exchange notices in Hardwicke's Science-Gossip
citation: Jean Tempère, exchange notices and responses, Hardwicke’s Science-Gossip 14–19 (1878–1883), beginning vol. 14 (1878): 72, 240, 264.
tags: France; Britain; Tempère; slide exchange; circulation; amateur microscopy; postal networks; provenance
note: A sustained run of exchange notices preceding Tempère's large commercial series. The notices document repeated circulation through Science-Gossip; surviving slides from this phase bear receipt dates, including July 1882, and later provenance in an American collection. This supplies a pre-commercial circulation layer for Tempère's physical slides.
links: Tempère reconstruction and year-by-year Science-Gossip references: https://microscopist.net/Tempere.html

title: Préparations microscopiques relatives à l’anatomie comparée et à la géologie
citation: Charles Marchand, “Préparations microscopiques relatives à l’anatomie comparée et à la géologie,” in Exposition Universelle Internationale de 1878 à Paris, Catalogue officiel, vol. 2, Section française (Paris, 1878), 34.
tags: France; Paris; Charles Marchand; commercial preparations; comparative anatomy; geology; exhibition; surviving slides
note: A direct exhibition record for Marchand's microscopic preparations in comparative anatomy and geology. Surviving labelled Marchand slides independently demonstrate the physical output of the business, so the entry joins an official exhibition description to extant objects.

title: Diatomées de Belgique
citation: Charles-Henri Delogne, Diatomées de Belgique, fascs. I–IV, nos. 1–100 (Bruxelles: self-published, 1880–1881), with 100 microscope-slide exsiccata.
tags: Belgium; Brussels; Delogne; diatoms; slide series; exsiccata; numbered set; surviving slides; provenance
note: A Belgian numbered diatom publication consisting of four fascicles and 100 microscope slides. Modern work on Delogne's surviving material explicitly uses the original exsiccata slides and associated handwritten sample list to recover specimen provenance and typify taxa.
links: Schuster et al. 2023 bibliography: https://www.nhm-wien.ac.at/verlag/wissenschaftliche_publikationen/annalen_serie_b/125_2023; object-based taxonomic reconstruction: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/341901607_Observations_on_and_typification_of_Navicula_fontinalis_Grunow_Naviculaceae_Bacillariophyta

authors: Henri Ferdinand van Heurck and Albert Grunow
title: Types du Synopsis des Diatomées de Belgique
citation: Henri Ferdinand van Heurck and Albert Grunow, Types du Synopsis des Diatomées de Belgique: Déterminations, Notes et Diagnoses par M. A. Grunow, séries I–XXII, nos. 1–550 (Anvers: édité par l’auteur, 1882–1885), with 25 microscope slides per series.
tags: Belgium; Antwerp; Van Heurck; Grunow; diatoms; slide series; numbered sets; subscription; object-text; provenance
note: One of the strongest continental object-text publication systems. Harvard reconstructs 550 numbered strewn mounts from slide labels and printed schedules; the Iowa documentary edition shows that the Types formed the physical-slide component of the Synopsis and were issued in boxed groups of 25 with explanatory pamphlets. Dating of actual slide distribution extends into the mid-1880s, while the bibliographic series is conventionally dated 1882–1885.
links: Harvard Farlow Herbarium: https://diatoms.hsites.harvard.edu/heurck-grunow; University of Iowa digital Synopsis: https://sdrc.lib.uiowa.edu/algae/VanHeurck/VanHeurck1/about.htm

title: Préparations microscopiques: histologie humaine et comparée normale et pathologique, médicale, physiologie végétale, diatomées, etc.
citation: Eugène Bourgogne, Préparations microscopiques: histologie humaine et comparée normale et pathologique, médicale, physiologie végétale, diatomées, etc. (Paris, 1884).
tags: France; Paris; Eugène Bourgogne; slide catalogue; histology; pathology; botany; diatoms; pricing; trade
note: A dedicated catalogue of Bourgogne's preparations covering normal and pathological comparative histology, medical material, plant physiology and diatoms. Contemporary American notice described many hundreds of preparations offered at moderate prices. The BnF catalogue independently records the publication.

title: Préparations microscopiques at the Exposition Universelle d’Anvers
citation: Robert Drosten, display of “préparations microscopiques,” Exposition Universelle d’Anvers (Antwerp, 1885).
tags: Belgium; Brussels; Robert Drosten; commercial preparations; bacteriology; scientific supplies; exhibition; slide trade
note: A Belgian commercial-preparation record centred on a Brussels scientific supplier and microscopist. Drosten's 1885 Antwerp display explicitly included microscopic preparations; an 1886 technical notice further reported that he maintained a rich stock of all kinds of microscopic preparations. Surviving slides bearing his labels supply an object-level counterpart.

title: Diatomées de France
citation: Jean Tempère and Paul Petit, Diatomées de France, numbered microscope-slide series begun 1887; Petit collaboration 1887–1893, continued with Hippolyte Peragallo to 1900; c. 400 slides.
tags: France; Tempère; Petit; Peragallo; diatoms; slide series; numbered sets; commercial circulation; exsiccata
note: A substantial French diatom slide publication distinct from the already-listed Diatomées du Monde Entier. Begun with Paul Petit in 1887 and later continued with Peragallo, the series reportedly reached about 400 physical slides and was advertised internationally.
links: Tempère reconstruction and period advertisements: https://microscopist.net/Tempere.html

title: Algues de France
citation: Jean Tempère and Lucien Dupray, Algues de France, microscope-slide series (1889–1892).
tags: France; Tempère; Dupray; algae; slide series; commercial preparations; teaching; circulation
note: A collaborative French slide series devoted to algae. It broadens Tempère's physical-publication programme beyond diatoms and is documented alongside his other named commercial series and advertisements from the period.

title: Champignons de France
citation: Jean Tempère and E. Dutertre, Champignons de France, 10 sets comprising 250 microscope slides (1892–1893).
tags: France; Tempère; Dutertre; fungi; slide series; 250 slides; boxed sets; commercial preparations
note: A bounded fungal slide publication of 250 microscope slides issued in ten sets. Its explicit physical extent makes it especially useful for comparing serial slide publication across taxa and for distinguishing a commercial series from general mycological literature.

title: Advertisement for microscopic preparations
citation: Eugène Bourgogne, advertisement for microscopic preparations, American Monthly Microscopical Journal (1895).
tags: France; United States; Eugène Bourgogne; slide trade; advertisement; transatlantic commerce; commercial preparations
note: A late nineteenth-century transatlantic advertising state of Bourgogne's slide business. Retained separately from the 1884 catalogue because it documents the continuing international market and direct solicitation of American microscopists more than a decade later.
links: Bourgogne reconstruction with reproduced 1895 advertisement and source list: https://www.microscopist.net/BourgogneJoseph.html

title: Farmaceuten og naturforskeren Carl (Charles) Hansen: et fragment af en livshistorie som bidrag til dansk naturvidenskabs historie
citation: Axel Garboe, “Farmaceuten og naturforskeren Carl (Charles) Hansen: et fragment af en livshistorie som bidrag til dansk naturvidenskabs historie,” Theriaca 7 (Copenhagen: Dansk Farmacihistorisk Selskab, 1961), 40 pp.
tags: France; Denmark; Carl Hansen; slide maker; microscopic preparations; diatoms; Paris; trade; scientific networks
note: A maker-centred study of the Danish pharmacist-naturalist Carl (Charles) Hansen, who settled in Paris after 1870–71 as a manufacturer and dealer of microscopic preparations and assisted leading Parisian scientists. Included because the preparation trade is central to the subject's scientific career rather than incidental.

title: Tempère’s artistic microscopic mounts
citation: Pierre Girodet, “Tempère’s artistic microscopic mounts,” Quekett Journal of Microscopy 39 (2004): 661–671.
tags: France; Tempère; artistic mounts; arranged slides; material culture; slide making; surviving slides
note: An object-centred study of Tempère's artistic microscope mounts. It complements the existing maker history by focusing on the construction and visual organization of physical preparations rather than simply biography or trade chronology.

authors: Tanja M. Schuster, David M. Williams, and Bart Van de Vijver
title: The diatom collection of Albert Grunow (1826–1914) at the herbarium of the Natural History Museum Vienna (W)
citation: Tanja M. Schuster, David M. Williams, and Bart Van de Vijver, “The diatom collection of Albert Grunow (1826–1914) at the herbarium of the Natural History Museum Vienna (W),” Annalen des Naturhistorischen Museums in Wien, Serie B 124 (2022): 331–362.
tags: Austria; Vienna; Albert Grunow; diatoms; surviving slides; catalogue; historical collection; exsiccata; provenance
note: A major reconstruction of Grunow's historical diatom collection at W. The collection integrates approximately 1,450 microscope slides with thousands of catalogue/sample entries and incorporates historical slide sets by Delogne, Eulenstein, Cleve & Möller, Van Heurck and others, making it a high-value provenance hub for the European slide economy.
links: Naturhistorisches Museum Wien staff bibliography: https://www.nhm-wien.ac.at/en/tanja_schuster; IMIS bibliographic record: https://www.marinespecies.org/imis.php?module=ref&refid=355596

citation: Tanja M. Schuster, Paul B. Hamilton, Verena Haring, Mark B. Edlund, and Bart Van de Vijver, “An introduction to the catalogue of Albert Grunow’s 19th century diatom collection at W including a palaeographic aid,” Annalen des Naturhistorischen Museums in Wien, Serie B 125 (2023): 101–122.
